_notes: The curated shelf: voices you can install, one entry per offer. App content, not library content — it ships with the code because only the engines in this build know how to install these. Every entry has a sample under samples/ that was rendered by the real engine at the 'natural' style, so a reader hears the actual voice before committing to a download, and installing a shelf voice is a file copy rather than a render. 'downloadBytes' is what a fresh machine fetches; an asset already on disk is reused and the install is instant. Add an entry: drop the sample in samples/, add the row here — no code change.

voices.name: Narrator
voices.description: Even and unhurried. The voice Story Mode ships with.

voices.name: Narrator (XTTS)
voices.description: The same reference recording as the built-in narrator, read by a different engine. Slower to add — it learns the voice — but it also speaks Polish, Russian, German and thirteen more.
voices.attribution: XTTS-v2 (Coqui, CPML) cloning the Chatterbox default voice, Resemble AI (MIT)

voices.name: Gosia (XTTS)
voices.description: A Polish speaker, cloned rather than trained — the first Polish voice here that is not a fixed model. Compare it against Bass before deciding.

voices.name: Gosia (MOSS)
voices.description: Polish, copied from a recording. The only voice here that is both cloned and permissively licensed — slower than Bass, far faster than Qwen. Short lines of dialogue can come out clipped.

voices.name: Narrator (MOSS)
voices.description: The same reference recording as the built-in narrator, read by the engine that also speaks Polish without a licence to worry about.
voices.attribution: MOSS-TTS (OpenMOSS, Apache 2.0) cloning the Chatterbox default voice, Resemble AI (MIT)

voices.name: Agnes
voices.description: Polish, female. A voice trained for Polish rather than borrowed from another language. Very slow — closer to an overnight job than an afternoon one for a whole story.
voices.attribution: Sticzu pl-Agnes, fine-tuned on Microsoft VibeVoice-Realtime-0.5B; inference code from the VibeVoice community fork (MIT)

voices.name: Marek
voices.description: Polish, male. Agnes's counterpart, and just as slow. Worth hearing them against Bass and Gosia before committing a story to either.
voices.attribution: Sticzu pl-Marek, fine-tuned on Microsoft VibeVoice-Realtime-0.5B; inference code from the VibeVoice community fork (MIT)

voices.name: Narrator (VibeVoice)
voices.description: The built-in narrator's recording, read by a model built for long stretches rather than sentences. Slow to start and then quick, so it suits a whole chapter better than a line.
voices.attribution: VibeVoice-1.5B via the community fork (MIT), cloning the Chatterbox default voice, Resemble AI (MIT)

voices.name: Gosia (Higgs)
voices.description: Polish, copied from a recording by the model that claims the best Polish of any here. It is also the slowest by a distance: a twenty-minute story would take most of a working day.
voices.attribution: Higgs TTS 3 (Boson AI, research and non-commercial licence) cloning OHF-Voice pl_PL-gosia (CC0)

voices.name: Narrator (Higgs)
voices.description: The built-in narrator's recording, read by the same very slow model. Here to be compared against, rather than to read anything long.
voices.attribution: Higgs TTS 3 (Boson AI, research and non-commercial licence) cloning the Chatterbox default voice, Resemble AI (MIT)

voices.name: Ryan
voices.description: American English, male. Warm and steady — the closest of these to an audiobook read.
voices.attribution: Piper voice en_US-ryan-high (rhasspy), packaged by sherpa-onnx

voices.name: Cori
voices.description: British English, female. Crisp and even.
voices.attribution: Piper voice en_GB-cori-high (rhasspy), packaged by sherpa-onnx

voices.name: Lessac
voices.description: American English, female. Clear and brisk; flatter than Ryan, easier for long stretches than for drama.
voices.attribution: Piper voice en_US-lessac-high (rhasspy), packaged by sherpa-onnx

voices.name: Qwen Polish
voices.description: A Polish-only model with one built-in voice — no recording to copy. Currently the slowest engine here by a wide margin; judge it on the sample before committing a whole story to it.
voices.attribution: agnostic/Qwen3-TTS-Polish, a Polish fine-tune of Qwen3-TTS (Apache 2.0)

voices.name: Bass
voices.description: Polish, male. The only high-quality-tier Polish voice available — try this one first.
voices.attribution: Piper voice pl_PL-bass-high (rhasspy), packaged by sherpa-onnx

voices.name: MC Speech
voices.description: Polish, male. A different reader from Bass and Darkman — worth comparing.
voices.attribution: Piper voice pl_PL-mc_speech-medium (rhasspy), packaged by sherpa-onnx

voices.name: Mai
voices.description: Polish, female. A different family from the others — no phoneme dictionary, so it reads the letters directly. Worth hearing against Bass.
voices.attribution: Coqui VITS pl-mai_female, packaged by sherpa-onnx

voices.name: Gosia
voices.description: Polish, female. Measured and even. Polish still sounds rougher than English — listen to the sample first.

voices.name: Darkman
voices.description: Polish, male. Low and level. Same caveat as Gosia — hear it before you pick it.
